can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying singular and plural nouns with an adjective after a determiner.
example_raw:
Martin is my best friend. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Slovak; Pass)

We have a big garden and a small swimming pool. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Arabic - Other; Pass)

Her favourite colours are blue and black. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Hungarian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Attaching a property to an entity that has been identified
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a descriptive word right before the thing you are talking about, after pointing it out.

positives: I have a big garden.
She loves her new car.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases with a limited range of determiners + singular and plural nouns. ► Nouns and noun phrases: functions
example_raw:
There is also a park near my house. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Pashto; Pass)

My husband is a teacher. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Korean; Pass)

That's why I like this place. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Urdu; Pass)

I go to college every day. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Identifying or singling out a specific entity or quantity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using pointer words like 'a', 'the', 'my', or 'this' before a noun.

positives: I like this place.
My husband is a teacher.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases by pre-modifying a limited range of nouns with another noun.
example_raw:
Every Friday I go swimming and play computer games. (Poland; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Polish; Pass)

I am having a dinner party on Friday 25 December at 7 pm. (India; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Panjabi; Pass)

Can you come to my house on Friday evening? (Iran; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Farsi; Pass)

My girlfriend likes vegetable pasta with tomato sauce, because she is vegetarian. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Polish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Combining two entities to create a more specific category of the second entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a noun like an adjective to describe another noun.

positives: I like to play computer games.
She makes excellent tomato sauce.

guideword: FORM: WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE AS POSTMODIFIER
can_do_statement: Can post-modify noun phrases by using a non-defining relative clause. ► Clauses: relative
example_raw:
She's in a volleyball team like me, but we're not in the same one. She was for the other team, which lost. (Switzerland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Swiss German; Pass)

You can always visit our Shopping Centre, which is one of the biggest in Brazil. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2001; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Adding supplementary details to an entity using a clause that does not restrict its identity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a comma and 'which', 'who', or 'whose' to give extra information about a noun.

positives: He played for the other team, which lost.
I saw John, who is my brother.
negatives: The car which I bought is red.
I do not know who she is.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying nouns with an increasing range of determiners.
example_raw:
There are so many shops, you can play games, eat food like Chinese food. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2001; Chinese; Pass)

I had so much fun! (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

I spent too much money, five hundred euros, but I don’t mind because they are beautiful! (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

I visited a lot of museums and I went shopping. (Argentina; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

All of our classmates were there and some of my cousins too. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Specifying quantities or identities of entities using a broader set of determining words.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using quantifiers like 'many', 'much', 'some', 'all', or 'a lot of' before a noun.

positives: There are so many shops here.
I had so much fun today.
negatives: Many of the shops are closed.
Much to my surprise, he left.

can_do_statement: Can form simple noun phrases with a limited range of determiners + uncountable nouns.
example_raw:
The food was delicious and the music was great. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Turkish; Pass)

The weather was so cold. (Philippines; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Chinese; Pass)

I phoned for more information two days ago. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Italian; Pass)

[talking about a book] It is very important because I need to do some homework in it. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Marathi; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Pointing out mass entities that cannot be counted individually.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using determiners like 'the', 'some', or 'more' with words for substances or concepts.

positives: The food was delicious.
I need to do some homework.
negatives: There is a lot of cars.

can_do_statement: Can pre-modify noun phrases with a limited range of more than one adjective.
example_raw:
I bought a beautiful pink skirt and a white top. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

Lysiane is taller than me and she has short black hair. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Portuguese; Pass)

It is a beautiful old city and there is the old wall around the city. (Latvia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Russian; Pass)

I left my small white bag. (Argentina; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Don't forget to wear old, comfortable clothes. (Peru; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using two or more adjectives in a row before a noun.

positives: I bought a beautiful pink skirt.
She has short black hair.
negatives: The shirt is beautiful and pink.

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADVERBS + ADJECTIVES
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases with adverb + adjective + noun.
example_raw:
It took us a very long time but it was a great fun! (Poland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Polish; Pass)

They made really good friends. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Intensifying or modulating the property of an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using an adverb like 'very' or 'really' before an adjective that describes a noun.

positives: It took a very long time.
They made really good friends.

can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases by using a prepositional phrase after the main noun in a noun phrase.
example_raw:
It was a beautiful red dress with blue flowers on the back. (Andorra; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; French; Pass)

Yesterday a TV company came to our school to make a film about Bavarian pupils. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

I don't spend too much time in front of the television, I just watch it twice a week and on Sundays morning. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

I received your letter and you asked me about the future of my town. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

I have to travel to Montevideo to see my doctor because I'm having some problems with my health. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Adding structural or relational details to an entity using a preposition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Following a noun with a preposition like 'with', 'about', or 'of' to give more details.

positives: It was a red dress with blue flowers.
He asked about the future of my town.

guideword: FORM: WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE AS COMPLEMENT
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases by using a defining relative clause as a complement to a noun phrase. ► Clauses: relative
example_raw:
The mobile phone which I bought yesterday is brilliant. (Russia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Russian; Pass)

The person who gave me it was my father. (Portugal; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)

The last day when we can see the movie is Thursday. (Romania; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Romanian; Pass)

I want to invite you to a pop concert that is going to take place in the National Stadium. (Peru; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

The music that I like is Rock & Roll. (Russia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Russian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Restricting the identity of an entity using a clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which', 'who', 'that', or 'when' right after a noun without a comma.

positives: The mobile phone which I bought is brilliant.
The person who gave me it was my father.
negatives: The mobile phone, which I bought yesterday, is brilliant.

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADJECTIVES
can_do_statement: Can form an increasing range of complex noun phrases with more than one adjective.
example_raw:
The Northeast is so beautiful and it's famous because of its white sandy beaches and the coconut trees. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)

Last weekend I went to São Paulo to buy some winter clothes. I bought a white hooded jacket, a blue jumper, black gloves and a beautiful blue scarf. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Portuguese; Pass)

Inside there were three samples of a nasty purple liquid. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I know your company are offering an exciting new service in our area. (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Chinese; Pass)

He had beautiful green eyes, short, curly, red hair and he was wearing an elegant black suit with a red tie. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

You can walk along the streets and eat typical Spanish food in good restaurants. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Spanish - European; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Providing detailed descriptions using multiple adjectives.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a sequence of descriptive words before a noun.

positives: I bought a white hooded jacket.
He had short, curly, red hair.
negatives: The hair was short and red.

can_do_statement: Can use possessive determiner ''s' with a singular noun.
example_raw:
It's my sister's jacket. (Uruguay; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I bought a red tie because next Sunday it will be my father's birthday. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

Yesterday about 8 pm, when I was coming back home from a shop, I saw two men near my neighbour's car. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Slovak; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Indicating ownership or association of an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using apostrophe S ('s) attached to a noun to show possession.

positives: It is my sister's jacket.
I saw my neighbour's car.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with 'such a' + adjective + singular noun and 'such' + adjective + plural noun, to give emphasis.
example_raw:
It was so terrible because I've never been in such a terrible situation. (Russia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Russian; Pass)

So it was really funny to hear from her after such a long time. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; German; Pass)

Thank you for giving me such a fantastic birthday present. (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Chinese; Pass)

Also, we both liked to read and that was why we were such good friends. (Taiwan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Chinese; Pass)

I had never worn such high heels before. (Albania; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Albanian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing the degree or quality of an entity.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'such' or 'such a' before an adjective and a noun to show strong feeling.

positives: I have never been in such a terrible situation.
We were such good friends.
negatives: I am looking for such things.

can_do_statement: Can use a clause with a present perfect or past perfect as a superlative noun phrase complement, to talk about uniqueness.
example_raw:
It has the best promenade I have seen. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Pass)

The best book I've read is "The Da Vinci code". (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Italian; Pass)

It was the best decision you had ever made. (Chile; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

We enjoy going shopping, walking and talking hour after hour - She's the funniest person I've ever known! (B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; ; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Describing an entity as the ultimate extreme within one's lifetime experience.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a superlative adjective followed by 'I have ever' or 'I had ever'.

positives: It is the best book I have ever read.
She's the funniest person I've known.
negatives: He is the tallest boy in the class.
I have seen the best movie.

can_do_statement: Can omit the noun after possessive '’s' to talk about a place which is familiar to the speaker and listener.
example_raw:
Last week I left my clothes at the dry cleaner's and I can't collect them. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Polish; Pass)

I have to go to the dentist’s. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

I'll be picking you up at eight o'clock near the McDonald's, OK? (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)

I'm going to be absent from the English class next week, because I am going to the doctor's. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

It's next to your grandma's. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Referring to a location associated with a person or entity without explicitly naming the place.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using apostrophe S ('s) at the end of a sentence or phrase without the noun it possesses.

positives: I have to go to the dentist's.
It is next to your grandma's.
